findings.title: Spawned flusher processes are never killed/terminated
findings.body: Processes are created via `self.mp_context = multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")` and `self.mp_context.Process`, whose instances are `SpawnProcess` (a `BaseProcess`), not `multiprocessing.Process` (fork-context class on Linux). The checks `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` in `_ensure_processes_alive` and `join` are therefore always False for real flusher processes, so `kill()`/`terminate()` never runs. A dead/hung process is replaced without killing the old one, leaking processes and leaving hung producers alive.

findings.title: Zero processes / division by zero when no shards assigned
findings.body: `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` can be 0 when `assigned_shards` is empty (e.g. rebalance with no partitions). The next loop does `i % self.num_processes`, raising ZeroDivisionError, or if there are no shards it silently creates zero processes/buffers so nothing is ever flushed while the consumer keeps running. There is no guard for the empty-assignment case.

findings.title: join() can leave flusher processes running on timeout
findings.body: In `join`, when the deadline expires the loop does `if remaining_time <= 0: break` out of the `for process in self.processes` loop. Remaining processes are then neither waited on nor terminated, so `join` returns while background spawn processes/threads are still alive, leaking them and holding Redis/Kafka resources. Every process should still be signalled to stop even after the deadline.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag name shard vs shards
findings.body: Flusher timers use `tags={"shard": shard_tag}` for produce/segment_size but `tags={"shards": shard_tag}` for wait_produce. The plural vs singular key split breaks dashboards/alerts that group by one tag name and creates a new metric series. The tag should be consistent.
